newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli provident funds reduce equity holdings.
newsitem.headline: Israeli provident funds reduce equity holdings.

text.p: Israel's provident funds sold their equity holdings far more heavily than their bond holdings during the wave of redemptions that hit them in July and August, Meitav Securities and Investments said on Monday.

"All of the five biggest provident fund management companies made a strategic reduction in their share holdings, and more than required by the level of redemptions," said Meitav in its quarterly survey of the provident funds.
Provident funds are popular long-term savings schemes with special tax benefits.
Meitav found that shares accounted for only 11.0 percent of the funds' much-reduced portfolios at the end of September, compared with 12.0 percent at the end of June.
Meitav estimated the five biggest fund managers included in its survey, which accounted for two-thirds of total provident assets, sold 750 million shekels in stocks during the June-September quarter.

The funds were forced to liquidate a considerable part of their portfolios in the face of net redemptions totalling 6.8 billion shekels during the quarter. Despite the big sell-off of shares, the impact of the redemptions was felt mainly in the bond market, where prices collapsed.
The vast majority of the funds' assets are invested in government bonds.

Meitav noted that the provident funds remain a major element in the stock market, but the combined holdings of the big five accounted for 9.4 percent of the market valuation of Tel Aviv stocks at the end of September, down from 11.1 percent at the end of June.

However, the funds concentrated their holdings in a few shares. Among shares traded in the Mishtanim Index, the funds held 19.3 percent of the registered share capital of Elbit Ltd, 17.1 percent of Supersol Ltd and 17.7 percent of Clal Electronic Industries.
Meitav said most of the funds shunned small-cap stocks, but nevertheless held big positions in Bayside Land Corp 5, Israel Corp 5 and Ispro the Israel Properties Rental Corp.
